item.description:
## The review panel is a column
Dragging the right-hand panel wide used to kill the app outright. It is now the third column of the window rather than an inspector, so the divider, the live resize and the remembered width are the system's: drag it to any width and it stays there, and the transcript beside it holds its place while you do.
## The panel stops acting on a pull request that has moved
Every button in the review panel goes away while its own action is running, so a second click cannot start a second commit or post the same reply to GitHub twice. Beyond that:
- **Ship** refuses while a fix round is editing the repository, instead of committing half of that work. - **Ship** and **Merge** check the pull request is still open, and tell you it has been merged or closed rather than failing with an error you have to interpret. - Switching pull requests clears the previous one's checks, mergeability, reviews and threads at the switch, so nothing you left behind is read under the new number. - **Fix**, **Confirm** and **Auto Fix** ask whether anything in the whole workspace is editing the checkout, not just the thread on screen. A turn running in another thread no longer lets a second engine loose on the same files. - The checkout button cannot start a second fetch of a branch while the first is still running.
## A rejected push has a way out
When git refuses a push, the panel used to offer one button that failed the same way however often you pressed it. There are three controls beside the error now: **Ask** sends it to the thread as a question, **Resolve** sends it with the intent to fix, and **Refresh** only re-reads git, for when you have already sorted it out in a terminal. Nothing force-pushes and nothing is granted — whatever the engine proposes arrives as a card like any other.
## Fix
- A fix goes to the engine you pinned in the composer. Reaching a limit on one engine and switching the thread to another no longer sends the fix straight back to the first. - The fixer is asked for the cause rather than the smallest change, and to carry the tests and comments the fix makes untrue — which is what tended to come back as the next round's findings.
## Quieter reading
- Timestamps in the review panel no longer tick and twitch as their digits change width. Rows show the time, and "Refreshed at 10:31" gives you "4 minutes ago" on hover. - A thread in the sidebar shows how long its turn has been running and then settles as the time that turn took, instead of a number climbing for as long as the app is open. - The transcript no longer decides you have scrolled away when the panel beside it was merely resized, or when a new message arrived under a stationary view. - The reviewing bot's own footer — "Useful? React with 👍 / 👎" and the link after it — is stripped out of findings, so it stays out of the reply drafted for you and out of the prompt the fixer is sent. - The pull request picker is ordered by number, newest first, so rows no longer reshuffle because something was commented on or labelled. You see this with "Show merged pull requests" on.
## Fixed
The Keychain authorisation panel no longer appears at launch in front of a window that has not drawn, which read as the app hanging. When it does appear, it names what it is asking for.
---
Requires macOS 26 with Apple Intelligence, and `claude`, `codex` and `agy` installed on your login PATH and logged in.

## Trust Mode
A fourth security level in the composer, at the far end of the dial, for when you have decided to let an engine finish a job and do not want to be asked again. It answers every approval request from every engine with no card: writing and deleting anywhere its shell can reach, pushing, publishing, merging a pull request, resolving a thread on GitHub, and a request to widen this app's own permissions. Entering it asks you to confirm once, and tells you what you are turning off.
What it does not change. Commands the app runs unattended stay sandboxed. Every answer still appears in the transcript, naming the level that gave it. And nothing is remembered: the level writes no rules and touches none of the ones you made, so leaving it takes every answer back from the next request onward.
A question a model asks *you* still comes up as a card at every level, including this one, because there is no answer the app could invent on your behalf.
## Auto Mode can ask a model before it asks you
Set an OpenAI API key in Settings, and a shell command Auto Mode cannot place inside your repository goes to a model for an assessment instead of straight to a card. If it comes back safe enough, that one call is allowed; anything less, an error, or an unreadable answer still shows you the card. Nothing is remembered either way, and every assessment appears in the transcript with the result it gave.
What never reaches the model: any program the app already has a rule about, so no assessment can allow `curl`, `sudo`, `git push` or a package install; anything whose arguments reach outside the repository; and any command line carrying something that looks like a credential. Leaving Auto Mode while an assessment is in flight withdraws its authority — the card comes back.
This does nothing until you set the key. Assessments are also written to a diagnostic log in your temporary directory; the switch for that is in Settings, beside the key, and it is on.
## Far fewer approval cards with Claude Code
A `cd` or a `PATH=` in one command used to leave every command after it in that thread asking for approval, on the assumption that the shell carried on. It does not: each call gets a fresh shell at the repository root. Commands after one of those are now answered by the rules of the level you picked, like any other. A `cd` *within* a single command line still counts, because there the shell really is shared.
## Fixed
Switching between pull request branches in the review panel could spin the app into a beachball and then quit it without warning. The inspector still keeps its width across a thread switch, as before.
---
Requires macOS 26 with Apple Intelligence, and `claude`, `codex` and `agy` installed on your login PATH and logged in.

Acqui Agents is now **Kulula**. Same app, new name and icon.
**If you have Acqui Agents installed, this update will not reach it on its own.** Download the image below and install Kulula by hand, then drag the old app to the Trash. Your threads, settings and approval grants are picked up automatically on first launch, and updates after this one arrive the usual way.
## You choose how much the broker answers for you
A security level in the composer sets what gets approved without a card: Always Ask, the default, through Auto Mode, which answers anything confined to the workspace. Switching back to Always Ask also cancels any standing permission an engine is holding on its own, so the level you picked is the level in force. Permission escalations, pull request merges and releases always ask, at every level.
## Shell commands are granted by what they run
Approving a command once no longer leaves a rule that a differently-spelled version of a different command can slip through — a grant now covers the program and the paths it touches, not the text you approved. Commands that only read need no approval at all. Every grant stays listed and revocable in Settings.
## Review loop
- The findings picker shows what is still open, and keeps up as findings close. - A fix you completed stays marked fixed. - When Auto Fix cannot start, it tells you why and offers to create the branch instead of stopping without a reason.
## Threads
Switching to another thread and back no longer loses the transcript or what the inspector was showing.
---
Requires macOS 26 with Apple Intelligence, and `claude`, `codex` and `agy` installed on your login PATH and logged in.
